title: Subnet Mask
description: The line that splits network from host
tagline: The line that splits network from host

sections.title: What It Really Does
sections.body: The mask MARKS where the network part ends and the host part begins: 1-bits = network, 0-bits = host. Your PC ANDs its IP with the mask to learn which network it belongs to.

sections.title: Same Network or No Direct Talk
sections.body: Two devices talk directly ONLY if their network parts match. If not, traffic goes through the default gateway (router). A wrong mask breaks communication even when IPs look fine — a favorite exam trap.

sections.title: Shortcut Trick
sections.body: Mask octet values always step like this: 128, 192, 224, 240, 248, 252, 254, 255 — each step adds ONE more network bit.
sections.tip: 💡 Exam tip: /24 simply means 24 one-bits in the mask. Count CIDR bits!
